topIssues.title: [L2CM] Add ProxyAdminOwnedBase access control to predeploy initialize() functions
topIssues.author: aliersh
topIssues.body:
**FMA follow-up (FM1):** As identified in the [L2CM FMA](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/blob/main/security/fma-l2cm.md), the L2CM upgrade mechanism clears the `initialized` slot and re-calls `initialize()` on predeploy proxies. If `initialize()` is open to anyone post-upgrade, an attacker could front-run or re-initialize with malicious parameters.

All predeploy contracts that have an `initialize()` function should use [`ProxyAdminOwnedBase._assertOnlyProxyAdminOrProxyAdminOwner()`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/develop/packages/contracts-bedrock/src/L1/ProxyAdminOwnedBase.sol#L101) to restrict who can call `initialize()`.

### Acceptance Criteria

- All proxied L2 predeploy `initialize()` functions are protected with `ProxyAdminOwnedBase` access control
- Tests verify that `initialize()` reverts when called by unauthorized addresses

### References

- [L2CM FMA — FM1: Re-initialization State Corruption](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/blob/main/security/fma-l2cm.md)

topPRs.title: chore(op-reth): introduce factory pattern for OpProofsStore
topPRs.author: dhyaniarun1993
topPRs.body:
**Description**

Refactors the OpProofsStore trait from a flat interface (where read, write, and init operations were all methods on the store itself) into a factory pattern with distinct transactional providers:

- OpProofsStore — factory only; provides provider_ro(), provider_rw(), initialization_provider()
- OpProofsProviderRO — read-only provider: cursor access, get_earliest/latest_block_number, fetch_trie_updates
- OpProofsProviderRw: OpProofsProviderRO — write provider: store_trie_updates, prune_earliest_state, replace_updates, unwind_history, set_earliest_block_number, commit(self)
- OpProofsInitProvider — initialization-only provider: bulk insertion of initial trie/account/storage state, committed via commit(self)

This mirrors the pattern used in reth's database layer where the store is a handle that creates short-lived transactional providers rather than exposing database methods directly.

**Motivation**

The flat API made it impossible to enforce transaction boundaries — callers could interleave reads and writes with no clear commit point. By separating concerns into typed providers, each transaction has an explicit lifetime and commit() is always intentional.

**Tests**

- [x] e2e tests

**Additional context**

This PR prepares the database layer for `memory overlay + async batch writes` improvements

**Metadata**

NA

topPRs.title: feat(op-alloy): add post-exec transaction and receipt types
topPRs.author: nonsense
topPRs.body:
Part of https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19779

---

This PR introduces a new post-execution transaction type intended to carry SDM (Sequencer Defined Metering) metadata after normal block execution.

The new transaction uses type byte `0x7d` (`POST_EXEC_TX_TYPE_ID`) and is modeled as a first-class OP transaction. The payload currently carries a `version`, the target `block number`, and `per-transaction gas refund entries`. The result is a deterministic, block-unique post-exec transaction format that downstream code can encode, decode, hash, serialize, deserialize, and surface in receipts.

---

In future PRs, I'll be adding:
- node CLI / runtime feature flags
- EVM block-level warming logic
- execution-time refund generation
- payload builder injection of post-exec txs
- replay RPC / debug endpoints
- devstack / acceptance wiring
